pages.title: Why are there two glasses at my place setting?
pages.snippet: Water glass, wine glass, mystery glass: a short guide to finding your drink.
blocks: A guest writes: “There are two glasses beside my plate. Have I accidentally booked dinner for two?”
Not necessarily. A single place setting may include a water glass and a wine glass. At receptions, staff may also prepare glassware before guests arrive.
Count place settings, not just glasses: plates, cutlery and chairs provide the context. A photograph of a table does not tell you which glasses were used.
If neither glass contains your drink, try asking the waiter. Staring meaningfully at the table remains an experimental technique.

pages.title: Two glasses, one gift box | The Toast Rack
pages.snippet: A boxed pair of wine glasses. For anniversaries, housewarmings and ambitious solo evenings.
blocks: Two matching wine glasses in a presentation box. Clear glass, slender stems, absolutely no ability to improve the wine.
Popular for wedding gifts, housewarmings and replacing the two glasses you broke while explaining how careful you are.
Gift message optional. “You already own these” is not currently available as a printed greeting.
Price: £18 per pair. Wine not included. A surprisingly common source of disappointment.

pages.title: Two glasses at once? | The Spare Pair Forum
pages.snippet: One pair on your nose. One on your head. Still looking for your glasses.
blocks: THREAD: Does anyone else keep two glasses on them?
MAGNIFYING_MARGARET: “Reading glasses on my nose, distance glasses on my head. I can see everything except where I put either pair.”
FRAME_OF_MIND: “Those are two PAIRS of glasses, Margaret.”
MAGNIFYING_MARGARET: “Thank you. I now have twice as many missing.”
MODERATOR: “For drinking glasses, please use the homeware section. This is the third time this week.”

pages.title: Fenwick green-check blazer | Marsh & Button
pages.snippet: Dark green checks, contrasting pocket trim and enough pockets to lose your own receipt.
blocks: THE FENWICK BLAZER — Forest green check with contrasting pocket trim. Available in several sizes.
For workdays, receptions and telling somebody you need to speak to the manager without actually saying it.
Our catalogue photograph shows one styling suggestion. Shirt, trousers and air of professional competence sold separately.
Check availability with your local branch. We cannot identify a customer from a photograph of a jacket. We also cannot identify our own regional manager without her name badge.

pages.title: Green checked jackets | Second Impression Hire
pages.snippet: Jackets for conferences, interviews and occasions that unexpectedly require an iron.
blocks: Need a green checked jacket for one evening rather than the rest of your life? Our smart-casual range includes several checked styles.
Hire includes basic cleaning. Please return the jacket, its buttons and approximately the number of pockets it left with.
Exact patterns and pocket trims vary by size and availability. Ask to see the actual garment before booking.
Customer names and booking records are private. “I am being very nosy” does not qualify as written authorisation.

pages.title: Caring for a checked blazer | Pressing Matters
pages.snippet: Wool checks, decorative trim and the mysterious contents of your pockets.
blocks: A green checked blazer with contrasting pocket trim may contain several materials. Check the care label before choosing a cleaning method.
Empty every pocket before bringing it in. Conference badges, business cards and emergency biscuits are not part of the garment.
Tell us about previous repairs or borrowed clothing. We can treat a stain; we cannot negotiate who pays for it.
All collection tickets must be presented at the counter. “It was green” describes both half our rail and the accountant after seeing the electricity bill.

pages.title: Someone went home in my green jacket
pages.snippet: A reception, two similar jackets and a pocket full of somebody else’s mints.
blocks: THREAD STARTED BY: SLEEVE_IT_OUT
SLEEVE_IT_OUT: “Came home from a reception wearing a green checked jacket. Mine was also green and checked. This one contains reading glasses and has much better manners.”
POCKET_SQUARE: “Try the venue’s lost property desk. Give them the size, lining and a description of the pocket trim.”
SLEEVE_IT_OUT: “Already called. They asked what was in my pockets. Apparently ‘potential’ is not specific enough.”
MODERATOR: “Please do not post strangers’ names or photographs. This is a lost-property forum, not a public trial with coat hangers.”

pages.title: Terrace dining | Hotel Miramar
blocks: The west terrace at
serves hotel residents, visitors and private-event guests. Sea views are included. The sea has declined to accept reservations.
Terrace service runs from breakfast until eleven in the evening. Please check with reception when a private function is taking place.
Lunches, afternoon drinks and group dinners are available. Our staff can arrange tables for small parties or larger receptions.
Please do not feed the seagulls. They have already reviewed the menu and consider themselves entitled to everything on it.
pages.snippet: West-terrace dining, afternoon drinks and private-event service.

pages.title: Before your stay | Miramar guest questions
blocks: DO I NEED A ROOM TO VISIT THE TERRACE?
No.
welcomes non-residents for dining and drinks, subject to availability and private functions.
CAN I ASK WHETHER SOMEONE IS STAYING WITH YOU?
We do not publish guest lists, room allocations or private bookings. Please contact the person directly. Looking concerned while holding a notebook does not change this policy.
WHAT IF I LEFT SOMETHING BEHIND?
Contact reception with a description, the approximate date and where you last saw it. “My dignity, near the dance floor” is unfortunately outside our storage policy.
pages.snippet: Terrace visits, guest privacy and the lost-property cupboard.

pages.title: Hotel Miramar | Coastline visitor guide
blocks: is a seafront hotel offering accommodation, terrace dining and meeting facilities. Its traditional seahorse crest appears on the hotel’s own website.
The terrace also serves visitors who are not staying overnight. Check directly with the hotel before making a special journey, particularly when events are scheduled.
This is a visitor listing, not a booking register. We can help you find somewhere to stay, not establish where your brother-in-law was last Thursday.
Our directory also lists The Mariner and Coral Crown Hotel. Please check the property name before sending a complaint about the swimming pool.
pages.snippet: Seafront accommodation, terrace dining and meeting facilities. Check details with the hotel.

pages.title: Hotel Miramar — worth visiting just for the terrace?
blocks: SALT_AND_PEPPER: “Can you visit the Miramar terrace without booking a room? I want lunch, not a mortgage.”
WEEKEND_WANDERER: “Yes, we went for drinks. Check with the hotel first if they have a private function.”
BISCUIT_INSPECTOR: “Nice view. A gull maintained eye contact with my sandwich for the entire meal. Very attentive service, wrong employee.”
HAND_LUGGAGE_ONLY: “Make sure you mean the hotel. My cousin arranged to meet us at the Miramar cinema. We gave the lunch four stars; he gave the film two.”
MODERATOR: “Hotel reviews only. No naming other guests or speculating about who they were with. The gull may be identified by its lack of remorse.”
pages.snippet: Lunch, sea views and one deeply committed sandwich thief.

pages.title: Miramar Picture House | Films & ticket information
blocks: MIRAMAR PICTURE HOUSE — an independent cinema on Station Road.
Two screens, evening showings and a concessions counter with strong opinions about outside snacks. This is a cinema, not Hotel Miramar.
Seat reservations are available at the box office. We cannot reserve a seat on the hotel terrace, although several callers have asked with admirable persistence.
Please switch off mobile phones during the film. Whispering “I am in the cinema” does not count as switching it off.
pages.snippet: Independent cinema on Station Road. Film tickets, not hotel rooms.

pages.title: Family stays | Coral Crown Hotel
blocks: Make room for everyone at
. Our family suites are designed for seaside breaks with children, luggage and the one toy nobody can sleep without.
An indoor swimming pool provides an alternative when the coast is doing its impression of a leaking ceiling.
Ask reception about room arrangements before booking. Writing “the quiet child” in the special requests box does not create one.
pages.snippet: Family suites and indoor swimming, with room for the favourite toy.
pages.imageCaption: Coral Crown Hotel — official hotel photograph

pages.title: Pool questions | Coral Crown
blocks: IS THE POOL INDOORS?
Yes. Our heated indoor pool is protected from the weather, though not from your uncle’s explanation of how he nearly became a competitive swimmer.
CAN CHILDREN USE IT?
Please check current swimming arrangements with reception. Children must be supervised; an inflatable crocodile does not count as a responsible adult.
ARE TOWELS A SOUVENIR?
No. Neither are the robes, the room key or the unusually reassuring receptionist.
pages.snippet: Indoor swimming, supervision and the disputed legal status of borrowed towels.
pages.imageCaption: Coral Crown Hotel — official hotel photograph

pages.title: Coral Crown Hotel | Stay with your dog
blocks: The
lists dogs as welcome. Check directly with the hotel about suitable rooms and any arrangements before booking.
Dogs welcome does not mean dogs welcome everywhere. Ask about dining areas and other shared facilities rather than letting your spaniel negotiate at the door.
Pack a lead, your dog’s usual food and something familiar to sleep on. If they prefer your expensive jumper, congratulations: they have already packed.
This is a dog-friendly accommodation listing. We do not maintain records of individual guests, human or otherwise.
pages.snippet: A dog-friendly seaside stay. Confirm room arrangements with the hotel.

pages.title: Coral Crown Hotel | Eastern promenade directory
blocks: The
advertises family suites, an indoor pool and private functions on the eastern promenade.
Its seahorse crest is part of the hotel’s branding. Seaside businesses are not obliged to choose different marine animals, however much easier that would make our directory.
The hotel’s functions page lists weddings, a Coastal Garden Society dinner and a junior sailing club awards ceremony. Consult the hotel’s own page for the published information.
Other coastal accommodation includes The Mariner and Hotel Miramar. Similar crests do not mean shared bookings, owners or guest lists.
pages.snippet: Family suites, indoor pool and private functions on the eastern promenade.

pages.title: Coral Crown — family break or competitive towel folding?
blocks: SUITCASE_TETRIS: “Looking at Coral Crown for a family break. Is the indoor pool worth packing three extra bags?”
JUST_ONE_MORE_BAG: “My children considered the pool the entire holiday. Apparently the sea was insufficiently rectangular.”
PAWS_AND_EFFECT: “We took our dog. Contact the hotel about room arrangements first. He approved of the bed, which is not the same as being allowed on it.”
FOLDING_PROFESSIONAL: “The towel animal in our room looked like a swan. By morning it looked like a tax dispute.”
MODERATOR: “Please keep reviews about your own stay. No photographs of other guests or children. The towel swan has declined an interview.”
pages.snippet: Indoor pools, dogs and a towel swan with unresolved personal issues.

pages.title: Breakfast & the residents’ lounge | The Mariner
blocks: Breakfast at
is served from seven. Please consult reception for current serving arrangements.
Our residents’ lounge is available for small meetings and family celebrations. Ask about availability before inviting everyone you have ever met.
For public quiz nights and music, see our events page. An empty table is not a reservation, however confidently your uncle places his coat on it.
Guests requiring a quiet breakfast are advised not to ask the quiz regulars what they thought of last week’s answers.
pages.snippet: Breakfast from seven, small meetings and family celebrations in the residents’ lounge.

pages.title: Finding us & guest questions | The Mariner
blocks: WHERE IS THE ENTRANCE?
Look for the brass seahorse sign on Quay Street.
overlooks the old harbour.
IS THAT A UNIQUE SYMBOL?
It is our sign, not a copyright claim over the entire seahorse population. Please check the hotel name as well as the animal.
CAN I CHECK SOMEONE ELSE’S BOOKING?
We do not publish guest lists or private booking details. “They would probably want me to know” is not authorisation.
I LEFT SOMETHING IN THE LOUNGE.
Contact reception with a description and approximate date. We cannot return “the correct answer to question six”; the quizmaster says it never left.
pages.snippet: The Quay Street entrance, a brass seahorse and a firm policy on other people’s bookings.

pages.title: The Mariner | Old harbour visitor guide
blocks: offers family-run accommodation above the old harbour. Its entrance is marked by a brass seahorse sign on Quay Street.
The hotel advertises breakfasts, small meetings and family celebrations, alongside public quiz nights and acoustic music.
Check the hotel’s current listings for event information. Our guide is an introduction to the harbour, not an exhaustive calendar of everything that happens near water.
Other coastal hotels include Hotel Miramar and Coral Crown Hotel. Similar nautical branding is common enough that we recommend reading signs before carrying luggage upstairs.
pages.snippet: Quay Street accommodation, a brass seahorse sign and the old harbour.

pages.title: The Mariner quiz — is “the harbour” ever the answer?
blocks: TEAM_LAST_AGAIN: “Thinking of trying Thursday’s quiz at The Mariner. How seriously do people take it?”
PENCIL_DOWN: “One team brought a clipboard. Another brought a substitute. Make of that what you will.”
QUIZ_ME_GENTLY: “We answered ‘the harbour’ to six questions. It was correct once. Apparently the capital of Portugal has moved inland.”
PENCIL_DOWN: “Check the hotel’s events page before going. This thread is not a booking service.”
MODERATOR: “No posting current answers, private guest details or photographs of someone else’s answer sheet. Yes, this includes zoomed-in reflections in spoons.”
pages.snippet: Clipboards, disputed answers and a team with excessive confidence in the harbour.

pages.title: Quay Street Trio | Acoustic music for small venues
blocks: The Quay Street Trio plays acoustic sets for lounges, small venues and private celebrations. Three musicians. Several instruments. One continuing disagreement about the van.
You can find us in The Mariner’s Friday music listing. Check the venue’s current programme before travelling; this page is not a live attendance record.
For enquiries, include your venue, preferred date and the space available. “Between the drinks cabinet and the argument” is not a stage measurement.
Please do not confuse us with the Harbour Quartet. They have an extra person and remain suspiciously organised.
pages.snippet: Acoustic music, small-venue bookings and an ongoing disagreement about the van.
